RepairOps-LLM ⊣ Repair Governor · generated by ictrepair.render-html from a real langgraph.graph/run* execution · 17 runs · 17 ledger facts · 7 HARD governor refusals across 7 distinct rules

What this page is

Every number, id, verdict and detail string below is the output of executing this repository's actor — ictrepair.operation/build compiled to a langgraph-clj StateGraph, driven through run*, with escalated runs resumed through the real interrupt-before #{:request-approval} seam. Nothing is hand-written. The build throws and writes no file unless the run produces at least 6 governor HARD refusals spanning at least 7 distinct rules — a console that showed this actor never refusing anything would be worse than no console.

This page supersedes a docs/samples/operator-console.html that was committed to this repository with no generator anywhere in the tree. That page described a robotics-safety console — missions, robot-1, a parcel delivery, grasp actions — none of which exist in this repository's domain, source or seed data. It was hand-authored, and it is replaced by this generated one.

Governor HARD refusals (7)

A hard refusal is un-overridable: no human approval and no rollout phase can release it. detail is reproduced verbatim as ictrepair.governor wrote it. Every one of these runs terminated at the :hold node without ever reaching a human.

Approver attribution — measured, not asserted

Each row asks the artefact the store ACTUALLY persisted whether it carries an approver-shaped key approval, approval-by, approved-by, approver, by, decided-by, human-approver, reviewer, signed-by. :actor is deliberately excluded: on a ledger fact it names the EXECUTING actor (op-1), never the human who approved (tech-01).

DISCLOSED DEFECT Attribution is lossy per effect in this repo, as measured above: 4 of 8 approved effects retained the approver, 4 lost it. ictrepair.operation mints the approver onto the record's :payload only; ictrepair.store/commit-record! then persists :payload for the assessment/set, assessment/set, media-screening/set, safety-screening/set effects but persists :value (or reconstructs the record from scratch) for ticket/mark-completed, ticket/mark-returned, ticket/upsert, ticket/upsert — so the approver is dropped there. This is reported by probing the artefacts, so it will read retained on its own the day the store is fixed. Not patched here: changing commit semantics is not a rendering task.

DISCLOSED DEFECT The graph emits :approval-granted audit facts carrying :by (7 this run), but ictrepair.operation's :commit node appends only the commit fact — so 0 of them reach the persisted ledger. Probing every ledger fact for approver-shaped keys finds none. The audit trail therefore records that a human was asked and that the op committed, but not who approved it. Disclosed, not patched.
